subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a Dedicated capacity proof-of-performance run for FintechCo: 

High-level SLOs you confirmed on the call:
- p95 latency for streaming responses: <= 250ms (interactive experience)
- sustained throughput: 120 requests/sec at typical payload (avg 600 tokens request, 150 tokens response)
- concurrency target: support spikes to 400 concurrent users with graceful degradation
- streaming: token-by-token streaming required; startup latency (time-to-first-token) should be < 120ms

Questions we need to validate in the perf run (we'll own measurement):
1) Preferred GPU family: you mentioned cost sensitivity and are evaluating Nvidia A10G vs A100. We recommend testing both A10G (cost-efficient) and A100/H100 (headroom) to observe tail latencies under KV cache churn and concurrency.
2) Typical prompt distribution: are 80% of requests short (<=200 tokens) and 20% long (>=1000 tokens)? Please confirm.
3) Any hard limits on batch delay? We assume we can use 10-20ms batching windows to improve throughput without exceeding latency SLOs.

Proposed perf validation plan:
- Redwood will run a 48-hour Dedicated test with:
  * Baselines on 2x A100 (reserved) and 8x A10G (reserved) to compare unit cost and p95 tail behavior
  * Synthetic traffic shape matching your call profile (we'll load from the provided sample trace)
  * Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, time-to-first-token streaming, tokens/sec, tail CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates
- Deliverables: perf report, recommended reserved throughput (requests/min & tokens/sec), sizing recommendation (node counts / GPU types), suggested autoscale burst profile

Next steps:
- I'll upload the perf harness instructions and a draft sizing spreadsheet (attached). Can you:
  1) Confirm prompt distribution sample by EOD Thursday (2026-11-02)
  2) Share any compliance constraints for a Dedicated test cluster (network rules, IP allowlists)

If that sounds good I can schedule the test for next week (Nov 8 start) and loop in infra for provisioning.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: fintechco-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), perf-harness-instructions.md (markdown)

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@fintechco.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt distribution: approximate split is 75% short (<=200 tokens), 20% medium (200-800), 5% long (>1000). We'll push a 24-hour sample trace to the Drive folder you shared by EOD tomorrow.
- GPU preference: cost is a big factor for us. We'd like to see A10G as the baseline (price-sensitive), but are open to a single A100 run to understand tail behavior. H100 is likely overkill for our budget today.
- Bursts/concurrency: our web tier typically spikes for ~30-60s windows during batch job completions — we need the Dedicated sizing to handle a 3x baseline spike (i.e., up to ~400 concurrent requests) without p95 > 500ms. If Redwood can recommend an autoscale/burst plan that keeps p95 under 500ms during bursts, that would be acceptable for now.

One ask: can you include time-to-first-byte / time-to-first-token metrics in the perf report? That's a critical KPI for our streaming UI.

I'll loop in our procurement if the perf results look good — procurement will want an estimate of monthly reserved cost for both the A10G and A100 configurations.









—Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Platform
FintechCo
emma.jones@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Emma — thanks for the clarifications, that distribution is helpful. A few follow-ups and what we'll run: 

1) Test matrix:
   - Config A (cost baseline): 8x A10G nodes, reserved pool, target sustained throughput 120 req/sec, concurrency cap ~300, autoscale burst to 400 for short windows.
   - Config B (headroom): 2x A100 nodes, reserved pool, target sustained throughput 120 req/sec, better KV cache locality and lower p99 latency.

2) Metrics we'll include in the report:
   - p50/p95/p99 latency (end-to-end)
   - Time-to-first-token (streaming startup)
   - Tokens/sec and requests/sec sustained & peak
   - GPU utilization and memory pressure (to validate model fit & KV cache behavior)
   - Effective cost per 1M tokens for each config (using your expected token mix)

3) Measurement methodology:
   - We'll run each config for a 12-hour soak then a 36-hour steady/chaos mix (total 48 hours) so we can capture steady-state and burst windows.
   - We'll replay your sample trace through the perf harness (instructions attached) and instrument with our tracing hooks.

4) Sizing recommendation (preliminary):
   - If time-to-first-token must be <120ms p95, A100 config shows ~20-30% better startup latency under high concurrency due to larger L2 and compute headroom. A10G can meet the 250ms p95 streaming SLO for typical load but shows wider p99 tails during KV cache churn.
   - Conservative starting point: 8x A10G reserved with burst pool of 2x A100 instances for heavy spikes. That gives cost-efficiency for baseline and headroom for tails. We'll validate with the run.

Next steps:
- Please drop the 24-hour trace into the Drive folder by EOD 2026-11-02.
- Aditya will coordinate infra provisioning and provide the exact instance types and estimated reserved cost numbers.

I'll start scheduling the Dedicated cluster for Nov 8 as a tentative start; we can shift if procurement needs time.

Best —
Marissa

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Looping in infra notes and quick checklist so we can be ready for the Nov 8 test window: 

Infra notes:
- Provisioning plan:
  * Config A: 8x NVIDIA A10G (g4dn-like) nodes, each with 48GB GPU, 1.2TB host RAM per node. Reserve network egress rules for FintechCo IP ranges.
  * Config B: 2x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) nodes for headroom tests.
- Reserved throughput: we'll configure the Redwood Dedicated pool to enforce a target of 120 req/sec sustained and allow autoscale to 360 req/sec for 60s burst windows.
- Batching: we'll start with a 15ms batching window and monitor p95; if p95 climbs above 250ms in steady-state we will reduce to 10ms for short requests.
- Streaming: we'll enable continuous streaming path with prioritized FIFO for small requests to keep time-to-first-token low.

Checklist for Emma/FintechCo:
- Drop sample trace (24h) in Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-fintechco-sla
- Provide prod IP ranges for allowlist and any corporate proxy/waf config by 2026-11-05
- Confirm procurement cadence for reserved pricing (A10G vs A100) — procurement contact if available

Deliverables & timing:
- Provision infra + smoke tests: 2 business days after we receive IP allowlist and trace
- 48-hour perf run: Nov 8-10 (tentative)
- Draft perf report: 3 business days after run completion

If Emma signs off, Rafael and I will coordinate the run and share access to the perf dashboard during the test.

-Aditya
